note: EMPTY, and that is a statement about the 9 guards in tools/dev/anti-vacuity-cases.json. Swept 2026-08-30: 90 test files both scan the tree and derive a zero-verdict from it. Each was run under three lenses — blank the bound root; blank that root's test files too; blank EVERY root at once so no inferred binding can explain a pass. 65 went red under at least one lens (proven non-vacuous), 19 could not be judged (their arm never started), and 6 passed over a fully blanked tree. Of those 6, four are the oracle's limit rather than a defect: three scan a temp directory they create themselves (no repo corpus to be vacuous about) and one is refilled by its own import closure, the same limit knobs-import-bundle is reported UNSUPPORTED for. One — repo-index-hygiene — derives every verdict from the git index and never reads the tree, so an emptied tree changes none of its inputs. That leaves ONE real finding, no-leftover-backup-files, now fixed and in the manifest. This CORRECTS the previous note, which reported '16 more vacuous guards' from an interrupted partial sweep: every one of those was a lens artifact of the kind enumerated above. A single blanked root cannot tell 'the guard noticed nothing' from 'the root it actually reads was left standing', and that ambiguity is what produced the 16.
